thing.text:
PONG

The table is the court.
Three of its walls are the
table's own edges. The
fourth, on the right, is
yours.

The ball and the bat each
carry their own program on
their own panel. Click
either to read it.

TO PLAY

1. CLEAR THE COURT. The ball
   bounces off ANYTHING on
   the table, so vacuum
   these four pads away
   with Dusty -- he gives
   them back -- and slide
   your own notebook into a
   corner. Leave the ball,
   the bat and the counter.

2. Set Speed to Instant.

3. Point at the BAT and
   press SPACE. Then at the
   BALL, and press SPACE.

Both keep going until you
press "." on them.

Move your pointer up and
down the table: the bat
follows.

Every time the ball gets
past you the counter goes
up and the ball starts
again in the middle.

NOTHING HERE IS NEW

[move | across | 1/55] moves
the ball. The EDGE reading
says which wall it is
against. The TOUCH reading
hands it a bird to whatever
it has run into. The pointer
device drives the bat. A +1
given to the counter's bird
counts a miss.

Every one of those was built
for something else, and none
of them has heard of Pong.

THE BALL'S TEAM

Nine robots that differ only
in what they expect in two
holes -- the edge, and what
it has run into:

  hit on my left or right
     -> flip the across step
  hit on my far or near side
     -> flip the away step
  far or near wall
     -> flip the away step
  left wall
     -> flip the across step
  right wall  -> count a miss,
     flip, start again in
     the middle
  anything else -> just fly

Flipping is a x-1 dropped on
a number, exactly as you
would drop one by hand.

The touching reading is a box
of two: WHAT, and which SIDE
of the ball it is on. Without
the side there is only one
way to turn, and a ball that
meets the flat of a pad turns
round and round against it.
